comment: Demolition plan sequence notes (Sheet 8, Block 9) do not address required safety clearances from transmission lines. Missing: (1) pre-construction safety meeting requirement ≥48 hours before commencement with Austin Energy; (2) barricade requirement 10 feet from all transmission structures, including guys and anchors; (3) warning signs under overhead transmission facilities; (4) prohibition on materials and spoils storage within the transmission easement. Current notes only reference Environmental Inspector meeting and utility abandonment.

Construction and staging plans do not demonstrate maintenance of a 25-foot-wide access corridor with minimum 16-foot vertical clearance along the full transmission ROW length. The transmission easement location is not clearly delineated on the Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan (Sheet 5), and no construction plan explicitly shows the transmission access corridor dimensions required by UCM 1.14.4.
applicableAreas: construction area adjacent to transmission easement

comment: Demolition plan general notes do not include a requirement for contractor to use extreme caution when working near at-grade utility appurtenances. While the demolition notes address tree protection, utility abandonment, and safety meetings, there is no specific caution language warning the contractor about the electrical utility infrastructure present on the site.

Cannot verify that staging and temporary spoils areas are not overlapping with transmission easement because the transmission easement boundary is not clearly delineated on the Erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan. While Sheet 5 identifies a 'Staging and Storage Area' and 'Concrete Truck Cleanout' on the western side of the site, and Sheet 3 notes explicitly prohibit materials storage within the transmission easement, the transmission easement location is not graphically shown to verify compliance with the separation requirement.

Water utility line shown crossing through H.2 Street Yard planting zone along Valley View Road where street trees are present. However, no root barrier boundaries or designated planting zone delineations are marked on landscape plan, and utility type (Austin Water vs. private service) is not specified. Planting zone design cannot be verified from available documents.
applicableAreas: Valley View Road frontage, Street Yard (H.2) planting zone

comment: Two critical recorded easements required by law are not depicted on site plan: Greenbelt Access & Use Easement (2010070731, 0.31 acres, NE no-build zone) and City of Austin Drainage Easement (2011021137, 0.130 acres, NE corner). Additionally, transformer pads lack required AE easement documentation: Pads 1 & 3 show only 'Vault Easement' (not AE easement); Pads 2 & 4 have no easement notation. No dedicated AE easements visible encumbering transformer locations.

Existing public water and wastewater utilities in Valley View Road ROW are identified for demolition/removal. New private utility service connections are proposed. Site plan does not clearly show whether new private utilities are routed through public ROW or relocated to private property or dedicated easements. Final routing and ROW status cannot be determined from available plans.
applicableAreas: Valley View Road public right-of-way, utility service connections

comment: Demolition plan shows existing public water and wastewater infrastructure in Valley View Road ROW requiring removal. However, specific method of termination at property line/ROW boundary (capping, plugging, complete removal, or abandonment procedures) is not documented. Demolition notes address private utility abandonment but do not specify how public utilities will be terminated per applicable standards.

Demolition plan notes require coordination with City of Austin for removal of power poles and electric lines. Existing overhead electric line shown on southern property boundary. However, no Austin Energy coordination letters, permits, relocation feasibility studies, or removal approvals are provided in available submittal. Power pole relocation coordination and compliance with clearance/access requirements cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Southern property boundary, overhead electric line

comment: Site plan does not include a note stating that the site lies within the Austin Energy service area. This is a required site-specific plan note per AEDC 1.16.0(7) for all sites within Austin Energy's service territory.

Plans do not include the required developer responsibility note stating that the developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to current Austin Energy Electric Service Standards, including conductor installation costs, and for coordinating with other utilities to resolve conflicts.

Additional Review Acknowledgement table is not present on the cover sheet. This table must list all applicable external reviews, approvals, and permits including: TxDOT permit, railroad permit, gas company permit, easement acquisition, county approval, water district or MUD approval, Texas Department of Health approval, TCEQ approval, non-occupancy letter, service extension approval, and Planning and Development Review Department approvals.

Austin Energy Utility (AEU) clearance or approval has not been located in the submittal package. No clearance letter from Austin Energy confirming service availability is present in the supplementary documents provided, though Austin Energy noted that the completeness check is complete.

Electric Service Planning Application (ESPA) approval is not documented in the plan set. While new Austin Energy electrical service is clearly proposed (transformers, meters, pull boxes, and underground lines shown on Sheet 21), the ESPA submission and approval status cannot be verified from the current submittal. ESPA is normally submitted after site plan approval per the regulatory exception; current status cannot be determined from available documents.

While Sheet 29 shows an addressing plan with all proposed unit addresses (Units 101-104, 201-206, 301-305, 401-405, 501-504, 601-604, 701-705, 801-806), there is no evidence in the submittal that these street addresses or unit numbers have been reserved with 911 Addressing/Address Management Services prior to site plan approval.

No evidence of an approved addressing plan from Address Management Services is present in the submittal. Sheet 29 shows an addressing plan layout, but there is no separate approval documentation confirming that Address Management Services has formally approved the addressing scheme. Note that an Address Validation Letter (AVL), if issued, is distinct from an approved addressing plan.
